newsitem.title: POLAND: Tombs devastated at Jewish cemetery in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Tombs devastated at Jewish cemetery in Poland.

text.p: Hooligans have knocked over 12 tombs at a Jewish cemetery in the southern city of Krakow, the third attack on Jewish property in Poland in three weeks.
"The incident happened at night between March 10 and 11. Hooligans toppled the headstones of 12 tombs," the Krakow provincial police duty officer told Reuters on Thursday.
He said the desecration took place at the old cemetery in the former Jewish district of Kazimierz -- where Steven Spielberg's film Schindler's List was made.
Most of the area's Jews were killed during World War Two by Nazi German invaders.

The devastation was the third assault against Jewish property in Poland in the last three weeks. On February 26, an apparent arson attack destroyed part of Warsaw's only synagogue and a week later windows were smashed at a Jewish Cultural Centre in the southwestern town of Zary.
The Polish government and all mainstream parties strongly condemn anti-Semitism but there are some tiny extremist groups hostile to minorities.
